newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed with slight losses on Tuesday as investor jitters resurfaced following the comprehensive shake-out on Friday and Monday's partial recovery.

The AEX index of leading shares began the day in buoyant mood, climbing around five points in early trade as investoers seemed to have shrugged off Friday's plunge, taking on board Monday's 80-point bounce on Wall Street.

But Dutch sentiment soon turned as bonds also lost their shine, weighing particularly on financial stocks but nervousness was quickly evident elsewhere. The AEX closed 1.57 points lower at 622.33, well below the early peak at 629.22.

Dealers said the recent volatility had introduced a cautious tone to trade and that investors were not willing to take on large positions and were quick to bale out given the slightest perception that the market was turning.
"What happened on Friday is fresh in everyone's mind. Noone wants a big position or to stay in too long," one dealer said.
A subdued but firm start to Wall Street trade on Tuesday did little to boost the Dutch market and the index stayed locked in negative territory all afternoon.
"There's been reasonable profit-taking at the highs and that's enough to keep the market under pressure," a dealer said.

Aside from the financials -- ABN AMRO and ING closed 0.80 and 0.50 lower at 109.20 and 58.50 respectively -- other index heavyweights ended with light losses. Electronics giant Philips finished 0.50 down at 68.60.
Oil giant Royal Dutch was under pressure most of the day, closing 1.90 at 286.10 guilders as the oil price dropped further in the wake of a resumption in Iraqi deliveries.
Dealers said news the company was to sell its Cressier refinery in Switzerland and embark on a major reorganisation of its European refining operations had had little impact on the share price.

Some firms managed to hold onto early gains, including food and drinks concern BolsWessanen, which remained the subject of takeover speculation despite denials from the company and the prospective bidder Britain's Grand Metropolitan. BolsWessanen closed the day 2.00 guilders higher at 32.00.
Smaller caps continued to do well, with Getronics and ASM Lithography both closing with healthy gains.

Computer services group Getronics, which announced late on Monday the purchase of the remaining 50 percent of RAET it did not already own, ended 2.90 up at 46.00 guilders. Getronics said the deal would have a positive impact on earnings per share.
Semiconductor company ASM Lithography was active, and following on from Monday's almost seven percent rise, put on another 2.40 guilders to 84.80.
Dealers cited talk of as broker upgrade and U.S. investor interest but added this had been matched by Dutch institutional selling and said the rally may not have much further to go.

Temporary employment group Randstad climbed 7.10 guilders to 85.50 after announcing on Monday it had reached an agreement with the FNV Services Union in a dispute over the way the company pays its part-time workers.
